item.text: {"chapter_reviews":[{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"The notebook generally distinguishes formal commitments, observed events, analytical assessments, and uncertain inferences. It appropriately labels the Taiwan “nuclear shield” proposition as unproven and the DPRK veto as adverse/disputed. However, the 1B.5 inference still lacks direct evidence linking Xi or the exercises to nuclear cover.","closed_system_silence":"High residual risk. The notebook expressly records opaque nuclear command, alert, incident, custody, and implementation systems; silence about accidents, dissent, or threats cannot support a favorable inference.","duplicate_reporting":"WD001 and WD002 are distinct claims from the same Arms Control Association article, not duplicate copies. WD003 and WD004 corroborate broad expansion but should not be treated as independent confirmation of each quantitative detail. WD013 bundles a CTBTO article with unspecified member-status material and should be split before reliance.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both favorable and adverse material were sought and retained: official NFU/risk-reduction, safety, AI, and safeguards positions versus expansion, Taiwan-channel suspension, and DPRK-veto evidence. The balance is incomplete for implementation and contrary accounts of the Taiwan and DPRK episodes.","missing_source_type":"Independent technical or institutional implementation evidence is missing: Pentagon/FAS detail and specialist work for command/readiness and nuclear-conventional entanglement; IAEA or other independent implementation records for safeguards/safety; Chinese-language regulations, personnel evidence, or credible specialist reporting for professional autonomy and enforcement.","official_claim_independence":"Most favorable evidence is Chinese official text and establishes declared policy only. WD003, WD004, WD009, WD010, and WD013 provide some external checking, but no independent source verifies military nuclear custody, AI/biosecurity enforcement, or whether Xi’s Ukraine rhetoric changed conduct.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Low distortion risk for the core record: adverse Taiwan reporting and UN voting evidence concern discrete public events, not complaint volume. Open reporting is nevertheless more available for Taiwan than for internal nuclear safety or command performance, so visibility is asymmetric.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Adequately framed at chapter level: nuclear exposure, Xi’s broad authority, inherited NFU/low-readiness baseline, and the Ukraine, DPRK, US-China, and Taiwan shocks are stated. Attribution remains weaker for specific PLA implementation and diplomatic actions; the record needs targeted evidence of authority or direction for the Taiwan and proliferation-related conduct.","supporting_evidence_ids":["WD001","WD002","WD003","WD004","WD005","WD006","WD007","WD008","WD009","WD010","WD011","WD012","WD013","WD014"],"unresolved_risks":["The nuclear command, custody, readiness, and accident-prevention record is too opaque to infer effective implementation from law, doctrine, or formal commitments.","Direct Xi attribution for the Taiwan exercises, suspension of channels, and any nuclear-cover theory is incomplete; broad authority supports proportional responsibility but not a personal operational-order claim.","The 2026 retrospective source for Xi’s November 2022 statement has no accepted contemporaneous independent corroborating record in the ledger.","The civil nuclear safety law does not establish weapons-system safeguards or enforcement.","The AI and broader catastrophic-technology material is declaratory; no independent 2022 implementation or outcome evidence is present."]},"chapter_id":"1B","defensible_evidence_estimate":12,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["1B.3: independently sourced 2022 evidence on nuclear command, custody, alert status, launch-on-warning development, accidents, and the applicability/enforcement of safeguards.","1B.5: attributable evidence on whether Xi directed or approved Taiwan crisis conduct, and independent analysis or records testing the asserted nuclear-cover relationship.","1B.7: evidence on 2022 nuclear/dual-use appointment criteria, adviser autonomy, inspection practice, and professional expertise independent of official legal commitments.","1B.8: a contrary or independently documented account of crisis-channel decisions and de-escalatory efforts during the Taiwan episode.","1B.9: independent 2022 evidence of military-AI, biological, cyber, or other catastrophic-risk safeguards in practice rather than policy language.","1B.6: evidence distinguishing the DPRK sanctions-veto decision from Chinese material assistance, enforcement practice, or other proliferation-relevant conduct."],"substantive_issues":["WD001 bundles a specialist analysis with a separate Xi report source in one source-claim unit; split it into stable, single-source claim units and provide the Xi-report locator separately.","WD013 bundles a 2016 CTBTO article with unspecified CTBTO member-status material; the continuing 2022 non-ratification fact needs its own precise locator/source unit.","WD008 relies on a later official retrospective with a non-precise section locator; the named contemporaneous independent corroboration was not preserved as an evidence unit.","Several chapter conclusions rely on official Chinese commitments without independent implementation checks, especially WD005–WD008, WD011, WD012, and WD014.","The current adverse record is concentrated in force expansion and two public foreign-policy/crisis events; it does not fairly resolve opaque internal implementation or provide enough contrary evidence for key favorable claims."]}],"global_findings":["One selected chapter was observed and is returned once;
